items.title: Subextremal Kerr exterior in length coordinates
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A mathematical Lorentzian metric datum on the subextremal exterior domain; it asserts no astrophysical realization or observational claim.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On the axis-avoiding polar coordinate domain, let $0<\theta<\pi$ and regard
$\phi$ as the circle-valued azimuth in $\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. Each
choice of an open real interval of length less than $2\pi$ lifting $\phi$
gives an ordinary local chart. In any such chart,
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

On any such local polar chart, its Boyer-Lindquist line element is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

references.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §5, PDF pp. 14-15
H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §§7.2-7.3, PDF pp. 93-96

items.title: Killing tensors and quadratic geodesic integrals
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure differential-geometric definition; no particular Kerr Killing tensor or irreducibility claim is made.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.5, PDF pp. 97-100
M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §§5 and 9-10

items.title: Killing-multiplier current and its observer density
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical contraction convention; it asserts no conservation, positivity, matter realization, or empirical result.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq\mathcal M$ be open, let $S_{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$, and let $X$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$. For
$X_b:=g_{bc}X^c$ and $S^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}S_{cd}$, define the
**Killing-multiplier current** by

$$j_X^a:=-S^{ab}X_b.$$

At a point $p\in U$ and for an observer $n\in T_p\mathcal M$ with
$g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future-directed, define the associated
**Killing-multiplier density** by

$$\rho_X(p;n):=-g_p(n,j_X)=S_{ab}(p)n^aX^b.$$

The current and density are defined for every such $S,X,n$. The definition
imposes no conservation equation, sign condition, or coercivity property.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §§7.5-7.6, PDF pp. 97-103
M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §10, PDF pp. 30-31

items.title: Lorentzian signature and time orientation of the Kerr exterior datum
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure geometric verification of the metric datum; no Einstein equation, black-hole uniqueness statement, or observation is asserted.
items.statement:
For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
for $x=(t,r,p)$ the product tangent isomorphism
$$I_x:T_x\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\longrightarrow\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R\oplus T_pS^2,\qquad I_x(v):=(dt_x(v),dr_x(v),d\pi_x(v)).$$
Using the sphere rotation field $\xi$ from the Kerr exterior tensor definition, set
$T_x:=I_x^{-1}(1,0,0)$ and $\Phi_x:=I_x^{-1}(0,0,\xi_p)$. Put
$A:=r^2+a^2$ and $q:=\gamma(\Phi,\Phi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

references.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §5, PDF pp. 14-17
H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.3, PDF pp. 95-96

items.title: Conservation of quadratic geodesic integrals
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Conditional mathematical statement about affine geodesics of a metric-selected connection; no physical trajectory or observation is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $K_{ab}$ be a smooth rank-two Killing tensor on a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. If
$\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ is an affinely parametrized geodesic on a connected
open interval $I$, with tangent $v=\dot\gamma$, then

$$\lambda\longmapsto K_{ab}(\gamma(\lambda))v^a(\lambda)v^b(\lambda)$$

is constant on $I$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.5, PDF pp. 97-100

items.title: Kerr horizon angular velocity and the ergoregion
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Geometric properties of the subextremal Kerr exterior and its regular horizon extension; no black-hole uniqueness or observational claim is made.
items.statement:
Let $T$ and $\Phi$ be the stationary and axial product lifts defined in
the Kerr exterior metric-properties lemma: for $x=(t,r,p)$,
$I_x(v)=(dt_x(v),dr_x(v),d\pi_x(v))$ and
$T_x=I_x^{-1}(1,0,0)$, $\Phi_x=I_x^{-1}(0,0,\xi_p)$, where $\xi$ is the
rotation field on $S^2$ from the Kerr exterior tensor definition. Both are Killing
fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. In the ingoing product coordinates $(v,r,p)$, the smooth field
$$\overline N:=\partial_v-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\partial_r$$
is timelike on the extension and selects a time orientation agreeing with the
chosen exterior time orientation. On $H^+$ one has $g(\chi,\overline N)=-1$,
so $\chi$ is its future null generator. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

references.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §§5, 9-10, PDF pp. 14-15, 24, 30-31
H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §§7.3 and 7.6, PDF pp. 95-96 and 101-103

items.title: Kerr exterior vacuum verification
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A local tensor identity for the specified metric; it does not assert that arbitrary stationary vacuum data are Kerr or that this metric describes nature.
items.statement:
For the specified Kerr exterior metric $g$, with $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and
$r>r_+$, the Ricci tensor of its metric-selected connection vanishes:
$\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$. This is a local geometric identity on the entire
subextremal exterior, including the rotation axis by smooth extension.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.3, PDF pp. 95-96; cited only for context, not as the local Ricci calculation
M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §4, PDF p. 12, Ricci-calculation discussion

items.title: Local Kerr Hamilton-Jacobi separation
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Local solution of the geodesic Hamilton-Jacobi equation on the axis-avoiding Kerr exterior chart; no global integrability through turning points is asserted.
items.statement:
On an axis-avoiding Kerr exterior local coordinate rectangle
$I_t\times I_r\times I_\theta\times I_\phi$, where each $I_t,I_r,I_\theta,I_\phi$
is a nonempty open real interval, $I_r\subset(r_+,\infty)$,
$I_\theta\subset(0,\pi)$, and $I_\phi$ has length less than $2\pi$ and is a
local real lift of the azimuthal coordinate, define the geodesic
Hamilton-Jacobi equation for a $C^1$ scalar $S$ by

$$g^{ab}\partial_aS\,\partial_bS=-\mu^2.$$

For constants $E,L,\mu,Q\in\mathbb R$, set

$$\mathcal R(r):=[E(r^2+a^2)-aL]^2-\Delta[\mu^2r^2+(L-aE)^2+Q],\qquad \Theta(\theta):=Q-\cos^2\theta\left[a^2(\mu^2-E^2)+\frac{L^2}{\sin^2\theta}\right].$$

If $\mathcal R\ge0$ on $I_r$ and $\Theta\ge0$ on $I_\theta$, then local
separated $C^1$ solutions are given by

$$S=-Et+L\phi+S_r(r)+S_\theta(\theta),\qquad S_r'=\pm\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal R}}{\Delta},\qquad S_\theta'=\pm\sqrt{\Theta}.$$

Where both radicands are strictly positive the branches are smooth. No
smoothness at a turning point or global continuation of a branch is asserted.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.5, especially equations (7.18) and (7.33)-(7.36), PDF pp. 99-103

items.title: Kerr geometric parameters and SI unit restoration
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Unit and parameter interpretation for the Kerr metric; it asserts no measured value, astrophysical source model, or observational result.
items.statement:
In the SI coordinate convention $x^0=ct_{\mathrm{SI}}$, the Kerr metric's
coordinate $t$ is the length coordinate $x^0$ (not the time in seconds), and
$r$ is a length; $\theta,\phi$ are dimensionless. The metric parameters $M$
and $a$ in the
Kerr exterior definition are geometric lengths: the associated physical mass
is $m_{\mathrm{phys}}=c^2M/G_N$, and the physical angular momentum is
$J_{\mathrm{phys}}=c^3Ma/G_N$. Thus $a=J_{\mathrm{phys}}/(m_{\mathrm{phys}}c)$
is the specific angular-momentum parameter. The horizon parameter
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$ has units of inverse length; the physical angular
frequency is $c\Omega_H$ in inverse seconds. The Hamilton-Jacobi parameters
in geometric units have dimensions $[\mu]=[E]=\mathrm{length}$,
$[L]=\mathrm{length}^2$, $[Q]=\mathrm{length}^4$, and
$[S]=\mathrm{length}^2$.

These conversions restore units in the stated framework. They do not assert
numerical parameter values, a particular astrophysical source, or an
observation.

references.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §5, PDF pp. 14-15
H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §§7.2-7.3, PDF pp. 93-96

title: Kerr geometry and hidden symmetry — Examples

items.title: Kerr geometry and hidden symmetry — Schwarzschild limit
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical limit and separation example; no measurement or claim about gravitational collapse is made.
items.statement:
At $a=0$, the Kerr exterior is exactly the Schwarzschild exterior with
Schwarzschild radius $2M$, and $\Omega_H=0$. Its Ricci tensor vanishes. The
Hamilton-Jacobi separation constant reduces to
$Q=p_\theta^2+L_z^2\cot^2\theta=L_{\mathrm{sph}}^2-L_z^2$, where
$p_\theta:=S_\theta'$, $L_z:=\partial_\phi S$, and
$L_{\mathrm{sph}}^2:=p_\theta^2+L_z^2/\sin^2\theta$. The axial Killing field
$\Phi$ also gives the reducible Killing tensor
$K^\Phi=\Phi^\flat\otimes\Phi^\flat$, whose quadratic integral is constant
along affine geodesics.

references.title: M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §5, PDF pp. 14-15
H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §§7.3 and 7.5, PDF pp. 95-100

items.title: Kerr geometry and hidden symmetry — negative stationary Killing density
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A local sign calculation for the canonical scalar stress tensor and stationary Kerr multiplier; it makes no stability or observational claim.
items.statement:
At an exterior point $p$ where the stationary Killing field $T=\partial_t$ is
spacelike, let $U$ be an oriented coordinate neighborhood of $p$, restrict the
real scalar-field model to $U$, set its potential to $V=0$, fix a coupling
$K>0$, and let $n$ be any observer at $p$. There is a smooth scalar field
$\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ for which the associated Killing-multiplier density
$\rho_T(p;n)$ is negative. Thus the density $\rho_T(p;n)$ is not nonnegative
on all scalar first-derivative data at $p$, so this multiplier cannot provide
a pointwise nonnegative density for all such data there. If a scalar field on
$U$ satisfies its scalar equation, its current is conserved. This example does
not assert that an on-shell field exists with the prescribed derivative.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Black Holes (Part III lecture notes, 15 March 2024), §7.6, PDF pp. 102-103
M. Visser, The Kerr spacetime: A brief introduction, introductory book chapter, arXiv:0706.0622v3 (2008), §10, PDF pp. 30-31
